long_biography.plain_text:
Information technology gave Ali Yıldırım Koç an operating brief inside his family’s diversified industrial group. After early financial work in New York, he joined Koç Holding in 1997, developing new businesses before leading its information-technology and corporate-communications functions. That career established an operating record separate from the family stake that underpins his wealth.

Board stewardship replaced group management as he became a holding-company director, then vice-chair, and took chairmanships across group companies in banking and industry. His vice-chair position is non-executive, and his directly held Koç Holding stake sits alongside the wider family’s much larger collective interest. The distinction matters: his current role is governance of a diversified family enterprise, not day-to-day management by a controlling personal owner.
